title: Lagaan Is Coming Back to Theaters for Three Days. Twenty-Five Years Later, It Still Has No Equal.
excerpt: Aamir Khan's Oscar-nominated cricket epic returns to cinemas on June 12 with a new trailer and a fan poster contest. For the diaspora, this is personal.
body:
There are films that define a generation, and then there is Lagaan.

On June 12, Ashutosh Gowariker's epic period sports drama returns to theaters for a limited three-day run, marking its 25th anniversary. The film will screen on June 12, 13, and 14, giving audiences one more chance to experience the story of Bhuvan and his band of misfits on the screen where it was always meant to be seen.

## A Film That Changed Everything

When Lagaan released in 2001, it did something no Hindi film had done before with quite the same scale or ambition. Set in 1893, during the height of British colonial rule, the film tells the story of a drought-stricken village crushed under impossible taxes. When a young farmer named Bhuvan — played by Aamir Khan — challenges a British captain to a cricket match, the stakes become existential: win, and the village is free from taxation for three years; lose, and the tax triples.

The film assembled an ensemble cast that became iconic: Gracy Singh as Gauri, Rachel Shelley as the sympathetic Elizabeth, Paul Blackthorne as the villainous Captain Russell, and a supporting cast that included Kulbhushan Kharbanda, Raghubir Yadav, Rajesh Vivek, and AK Hangal. Each character has become shorthand in Indian pop culture. Twenty-five years on, people still debate Kachra's bowling and Lakha's betrayal as though they happened last week.

The music, composed by A.R. Rahman, remains one of the greatest Bollywood soundtracks ever recorded. "Ghanan Ghanan," "Mitwa," "Radha Kaise Na Jale," and "O Rey Chhori" are not just songs — for anyone who grew up in an Indian household, they are sense memory.

## The Oscar That Almost Was

Lagaan became only the third Indian film ever nominated for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film. It did not win — the Oscar went to the Bosnian film No Man's Land that year — but the nomination itself was a watershed moment. For Indians living abroad, it was the first time many felt their cinema acknowledged at the highest level of global recognition. The film swept the 47th Filmfare Awards and won multiple National Film Awards, but the Academy nod is what put it on the international map.

## Why the Diaspora Should Care

For NRIs who grew up watching Lagaan on DVD or VHS, the re-release is not just nostalgia. It is a chance to take your kids to see the film that made you proud to be Indian in a room full of strangers. The themes of colonial resistance, community, and self-belief have not aged a day. If anything, they hit differently now.

Aamir Khan Productions has launched a creative campaign called #LagaanPosterChallenge, encouraging fans to reinterpret the film's iconic poster in their own style. Winners will be invited to a special screening with the original cast and crew — a remarkable gesture that acknowledges how deeply the film's audience has carried it forward.

## The Bigger Picture

The re-release also comes at a fascinating moment in Aamir Khan's career. He has reportedly locked dates for a new period sports drama with Gowariker — a biopic of legendary Indian cricketer Lala Amarnath, centered on the historic 1952 India-Pakistan Test series. Farhan Akhtar is confirmed in a pivotal role, and shooting is expected to begin by October 2026. If Lagaan was about cricket as revolution, the Lala Amarnath film promises to be about cricket as nation-building in a newly partitioned subcontinent.

For now, though, the focus is on June 12. Three days. One film. And a reminder that the best stories do not expire.

Lagaan screens in theaters on June 12, 13, and 14, 2026. A new anniversary trailer is available on the Aamir Khan Productions YouTube channel.
